title: The Mitochondrial Gate: BCL-2 and Cytochrome c

scenes.visual: Deep slate background (#0F172A), matching the first film. A large glowing teal (#14B8A6) schematic mitochondrion sits inside the same cool grey-blue (#94A3B8) cell outline, filling 70% of frame height with slow ambient shimmer. Crisp white title 'The Mitochondrial Gate: BCL-2 and Cytochrome c' (size 36) settles cleanly above it with no subtitle.

scenes.tts: The first film showed an outside death receptor building a platform to gather caspase eight. What if danger starts inside the cell, like damaged D N A, with no outside signal? Inside the cell, the platform's two parts are kept in separate rooms so nothing fires by mistake.
scenes.caption: The first film showed an outside death receptor building a platform to gather caspase-8. What if danger starts inside the cell, like damaged DNA, with no outside signal? Inside the cell, the platform's two parts are kept in separate rooms so nothing fires by mistake.
scenes.visual: Starts with the same schematic cell from the first film: the violet Fas / cyan FADD DISC sits briefly and dimmed at the upper plasma membrane, then the camera smoothly glides inward toward the glowing teal (#14B8A6) mitochondrion filling 65% of the frame. A subtle interior pulse marks damaged DNA in the dimmed nucleus corner while two labelled zones light up: 'Cytosol' outside the teal shell and 'Intermembrane space' inside.
scenes.narration: The first film showed an outside death receptor building a platform to gather caspase-8. What if danger starts inside the cell, like damaged DNA, with no outside signal? Inside the cell, the platform's two parts are kept in separate rooms so nothing fires by mistake.

scenes.tts: One part, a protein called Apaf one, floats folded and quiet in the cytosol. Its partner is cytochrome c, the small protein that normally carries electrons inside mitochondria. Keeping cytochrome c locked behind the outer mitochondrial membrane stops any platform from forming. Here, escaping that room is the death signal.
scenes.caption: One part, a protein called APAF-1, floats folded and quiet in the cytosol. Its partner is cytochrome c, the small protein that normally carries electrons inside mitochondria. Keeping cytochrome c locked behind the outer mitochondrial membrane stops any platform from forming. Here, escaping that room is the death signal.
scenes.visual: In the cytosol outside the teal (#14B8A6) outer membrane, compact folded indigo (#818CF8) blocks labelled 'APAF-1' drift calmly. Sealed inside the teal intermembrane space, bright golden-yellow (#FACC15) spheres labelled 'Cytochrome c' shuttle along the inner membrane curve. A solid teal boundary glows between them, clearly keeping indigo APAF-1 and golden cytochrome c separated. Labels size 30, white (#F8FAFC).
scenes.narration: One part, a protein called APAF-1, floats folded and quiet in the cytosol. Its partner is cytochrome c, the small protein that normally carries electrons inside mitochondria. Keeping cytochrome c locked behind the outer mitochondrial membrane stops any platform from forming. Here, escaping that room is the death signal.

scenes.tts: A protein family named after B C L two controls that outer membrane. It has three classes. Effectors called Bax and Bak can open pores in the membrane. Guards like B C L two hold them in check, gripping them in a surface groove. Sensors share only one short helix with the family, called B H three, which fits that groove.
scenes.caption: A protein family named after BCL-2 controls that outer membrane. It has three classes. Effectors called BAX and BAK can open pores in the membrane. Guards like BCL-2 hold them in check, gripping them in a surface groove. Sensors share only one short helix with the family, called BH3, which fits that groove.
scenes.visual: Camera zooms smoothly onto the curved teal (#14B8A6) outer mitochondrial membrane (filling 70% of height). Three colour-coded schematic classes appear along the membrane: coral-orange (#FB923C) 'Effectors (BAX, BAK)' capable of spanning the membrane; royal-blue (#3B82F6) 'Guards (BCL-2)' with a visible curved pocket clamping each coral effector; and bright amber-yellow (#F59E0B) wedge-shaped 'Sensors (BH3-only)' approaching from the cytosol, their wedge tip matching the blue groove. Tag 'Schematic' (size 24).
scenes.narration: A protein family named after BCL-2 controls that outer membrane. It has three classes. Effectors called BAX and BAK can open pores in the membrane. Guards like BCL-2 hold them in check, gripping them in a surface groove. Sensors share only one short helix with the family, called BH3, which fits that groove.

scenes.tts: Notice the double negative: sensors promote death by blocking the guards that restrain Bax and Bak. Some sensors can also activate Bax and Bak directly. Now suppose mild stress makes a few sensors, fewer than the spare guards waiting on the membrane. Pause and predict: does the outer membrane open yet?
scenes.caption: Notice the double negative: sensors promote death by blocking the guards that restrain BAX and BAK. Some sensors can also activate BAX and BAK directly. Now suppose mild stress makes a few sensors, fewer than the spare guards waiting on the membrane. Pause and predict: does the outer membrane open yet?
scenes.visual: Along the teal (#14B8A6) outer membrane sit five royal-blue (#3B82F6) guards: two clamp coral (#FB923C) effectors, and three have empty open grooves ('Spare guards'). Only two amber (#F59E0B) sensor wedges drift in from the cytosol toward the blue grooves. At top, a crisp white question banner settles: 'Fewer sensors than spare guards: does the membrane open yet?' (size 30).
scenes.narration: Notice the double negative: sensors promote death by blocking the guards that restrain BAX and BAK. Some sensors can also activate BAX and BAK directly. Now suppose mild stress makes a few sensors, fewer than the spare guards waiting on the membrane. Pause and predict: does the outer membrane open yet?

scenes.visual: Hold the question banner 'Fewer sensors than spare guards: does the membrane open yet?' cleanly at top. The two amber (#F59E0B) sensor wedges hover gently beside the three open royal-blue (#3B82F6) guard grooves while the two clamped coral (#FB923C) effectors pulse slowly inside their guards and golden cytochrome c (#FACC15) shimmers behind the closed teal membrane. Subtle 4.5-second progress bar along bottom.

scenes.tts: Not yet. Spare guards soak up that small wave of sensors, so Bax and Bak stay clamped. That buffer protects the cell from minor noise. When sustained stress makes enough sensors to fill the guards, Bax and Bak break free. They assemble into pores and open the outer mitochondrial membrane.
scenes.caption: Not yet. Spare guards soak up that small wave of sensors, so BAX and BAK stay clamped. That buffer protects the cell from minor noise. When sustained stress makes enough sensors to fill the guards, BAX and BAK break free. They assemble into pores and open the outer mitochondrial membrane.
scenes.visual: Question banner clears. The two amber (#F59E0B) sensors snap into two spare blue (#3B82F6) guards; the teal membrane stays sealed. Then a dense wave of amber sensors floods in, filling every blue groove and displacing the coral (#FB923C) effectors. Freed coral BAX and BAK dive into the teal outer membrane and assemble into wide open pores (schematic).
scenes.narration: Not yet. Spare guards soak up that small wave of sensors, so BAX and BAK stay clamped. That buffer protects the cell from minor noise. When sustained stress makes enough sensors to fill the guards, BAX and BAK break free. They assemble into pores and open the outer mitochondrial membrane.

scenes.tts: Through those openings, cytochrome c pours out into the cytosol. With the nucleotide D A T P, it makes seven copies of Apaf one open up and join into a wheel. That seven-spoke wheel is the apoptosome. Just like the surface disc, its hub gathers caspase nine, whose paired copies then cut and unlock executioners.
scenes.caption: Through those openings, cytochrome c pours out into the cytosol. With the nucleotide dATP, it makes seven copies of APAF-1 open up and join into a wheel. That seven-spoke wheel is the apoptosome. Just like the surface DISC, its hub gathers caspase-9, whose paired copies then cut and unlock executioners.
scenes.visual: Golden (#FACC15) cytochrome c spheres stream through the coral pores into the cytosol. Each docks onto a folded indigo (#818CF8) APAF-1 alongside a small mint (#34D399) 'dATP' chip. Seven indigo arms open up and snap symmetrically into a glowing 7-spoke wheel ('Apoptosome', size 32). At the central hub, muted crimson-rose (#FB7185) 'Procaspase-9' chains gather, pair up, flare vivid red (#EF4444), and clip muted orange (#FDBA74) executioner dimers into active amber-red (#F97316) cutters (exact same colours as Film 1).
scenes.narration: Through those openings, cytochrome c pours out into the cytosol. With the nucleotide dATP, it makes seven copies of APAF-1 open up and join into a wheel. That seven-spoke wheel is the apoptosome. Just like the surface DISC, its hub gathers caspase-9, whose paired copies then cut and unlock executioners.

scenes.tts: The outside and inside routes also connect. Active caspase eight from the surface platform can cut a sensor named Bid. Cut Bid travels to the mitochondrion and helps trigger Bax and Bak. That pulls the mitochondrial gate into the response. Inside, guards, sensors, and effectors together set the threshold.
scenes.caption: The outside and inside routes also connect. Active caspase-8 from the surface platform can cut a sensor named BID. Cut BID travels to the mitochondrion and helps trigger BAX and BAK. That pulls the mitochondrial gate into the response. Inside, guards, sensors, and effectors together set the threshold.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls slightly back to show both platforms in the same cell. From the upper violet/cyan DISC corner, a vivid red (#EF4444) active caspase-8 clips an amber (#F59E0B) 'BID' block; the cut piece glides downward to the teal outer membrane, engaging guards and coral (#FB923C) BAX/BAK to reinforce the opening and golden cytochrome c (#FACC15) release.
scenes.narration: The outside and inside routes also connect. Active caspase-8 from the surface platform can cut a sensor named BID. Cut BID travels to the mitochondrion and helps trigger BAX and BAK. That pulls the mitochondrial gate into the response. Inside, guards, sensors, and effectors together set the threshold.

scenes.tts: So the outer membrane usually gives way only after sensors fill the free guards. Once sensors tip the scale, cytochrome c escapes, the wheel assembles, and irreversible cutting begins. In the end, the B C L two family balance decides whether mitochondria release cytochrome c.
scenes.caption: So the outer membrane usually gives way only after sensors fill the free guards. Once sensors tip the scale, cytochrome c escapes, the wheel assembles, and irreversible cutting begins. In the end, the BCL-2 family balance decides whether mitochondria release cytochrome c.
scenes.visual: A clean schematic balance beam overlays the teal outer membrane (labelled 'Schematic' in corner): royal-blue (#3B82F6) 'Guards' weigh against amber (#F59E0B) 'Sensors' plus coral (#FB923C) 'Effectors'. Amber sensors pile on one by one until they tip the scale, opening the membrane as golden cytochrome c (#FACC15) flows toward the glowing indigo apoptosome.
scenes.narration: So the outer membrane usually gives way only after sensors fill the free guards. Once sensors tip the scale, cytochrome c escapes, the wheel assembles, and irreversible cutting begins. In the end, the BCL-2 family balance decides whether mitochondria release cytochrome c.
